pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Large, reddish-brown polygonal regions with irregular, serrated margins. The transition between dark and light pixels is sharp. The patches are non-uniform in shape, resembling complex leaf-like geometries with high spatial dominance over the neck and shoulder area.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: The negative-space lattice consists of cream-colored pathways forming a continuous interconnected mesh. Junction nodes typically consist of three-way intersections. The pixel thickness of these corridors is relatively consistent, approximately 10-15% of the average patch diameter.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: The mane exhibits a short, bristly profile with a high-frequency, low-amplitude serrated silhouette against the out-of-focus background. The texture is composed of dense, dark brown vertical hair clusters.
dorsal_ridge_profile.contour_gaps: A notable thinning and height reduction in the mane profile is visible at the anatomical transition from the dorsal neck to the shoulder ridge.

other_distinctive_markers: A Red-billed Oxpecker (Buphagus erythrorhynchus) is perched on the dorsal-lateral region of the shoulder, creating a localized occlusion of the pelage pattern.
